# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.

शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).

Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

Priyadarshini Scheme (Free KSRTC Bus Travel for Women)
Transport Department, Government of Kerala — Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC)

Since 15 June 2026, women and transgender persons travel free on KSRTC ordinary buses in Kerala, with no limit on distance. There is no form, card or registration, and no ID is needed: tell the conductor where you are going and take the zero-fare Priyadarshini ticket. Fast Passenger, City Fast and higher-class buses, festival and weekend specials and chartered trips are not free.

State Crop Insurance Scheme and Crop-Loss Relief (AIMS)
Department of Agriculture Development and Farmers' Welfare, Government of Kerala, through Krishi Bhavans

Kerala's own crop insurance. For a small premium, such as Rs.2 a year for a yielding coconut tree or Re.1 a cent for paddy, you get fixed compensation if the crop is fully destroyed by flood, drought, landslide, storm, lightning, sea erosion, wildfire or wild animals; paddy is also covered against pests and disease. You apply and pay on the AIMS portal or app, and the Krishi Bhavan checks the field. Farmers without insurance can still claim the smaller natural-calamity relief on AIMS, for example Rs.700 for a yielding coconut tree. In March 2026 papaya, rambutan and other fruits, flowers and bee boxes were added.
For total loss: Rs.2,000 per yielding coconut tree, Rs.35,000 per hectare of paddy, Rs.300 per bunched Nendran banana
Any farmer in Kerala who cultivates own or leased land. Paddy farmers can also join as a padasekharam group
Minimum to insure: 10 coconut or arecanut trees, 10 banana plants, 25 rubber trees, or 0.1 hectare (about 25 cents) of paddy
Insure within the crop's window: paddy 15 to 45 days after sowing or transplanting, banana 1 to 5 months after planting; yielding tree crops at any time
Insure the whole crop in that plot, not part of it. Old or low-yielding trees are not accepted

Cover starts 7 days after the premium is paid. Only total loss is paid: paddy loss above 50% counts as total, and for vegetables, ginger, tapioca and similar crops at least 10% of the insured area must be lost
Aadhaar card and the mobile number linked to it, for the OTP

Ladakh Universal Health Care Scheme (Golden Card)

Ladakh's own free health insurance, started in December 2020 alongside Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY so that families left out of the PM-JAY list are covered too. Every ration card household gets a Golden Card worth Rs.5 lakh a year for hospital treatment, tests and medicines, cashless at empanelled hospitals. The card is made at the Ayushman desk of a government hospital, at an enrolment camp or at a CSC, using the ration card and Aadhaar.

Every family in UT Ladakh that holds a ration card

No income limit and no premium

UT of Lakshadweep State Pension Scheme (Old Age Pension)
Social Welfare & Tribal Affairs Department, Lakshadweep (through the District Panchayat and Village (Dweep) Panchayats)

Lakshadweep pays Rs.1,500 a month to permanent residents above 60 who have no income of their own. The same state pension also covers widows, abandoned people and persons with disabilities. You apply at your island's Village (Dweep) Panchayat office. The application is checked there and again at the District Panchayat, Kavaratti, and the money is paid every month into your Aadhaar-linked bank account. About 3,500 islanders get it.

Above 60 years of age (the same scheme also covers widows, abandoned persons and persons with disabilities)
No source of income; monthly income not above Rs.1,500
Not getting any other similar government pension

Bank passbook of an Aadhaar-linked account in your own name

Department of Social Justice and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Madhya Pradesh

The state gives Rs 55,000 for each bride who marries at a mass wedding held by a Janpad Panchayat or urban body on a date the district fixes. The bride gets Rs 49,000 by an account payee cheque in her name, and Rs 6,000 goes to the body that holds the event. The Nikah scheme gives the same help at mass nikah events. There is no income limit, but a wedding held on its own does not qualify.
Rs 55,000 per bride: Rs 49,000 cheque to the bride + Rs 6,000 to the organiser
The bride or her parents are original residents of Madhya Pradesh (the groom may be from another state)

The bride is unmarried, a widow (Kalyani) or a legally divorced woman, and has not already married in another ceremony
No income limit, but the marriage must take place at a mass wedding or nikah held by a Janpad Panchayat or municipal body on a notified date
Registered construction workers also get this help through the same mass weddings; there is no separate grant for a wedding held on its own
